title: Durable memory
requirement: Keep scoped decisions, handoffs and useful learning available across native Codex and Claude with inspectable capture, deletion and recovery.
slot_question: Which single system owns durable memory for both Claude Code and Codex on the new host? Exactly one is installed.
a_deciding_comparison_would_measure: Run source-grounded recall and abstention cases with scoped capture, useful-write quality, deletion and isolated restore; compare complete usage without duplicating memory owners.
target_hosts: Primary: a new WSL2 Ubuntu-family instance on a Windows workstation, x86_64, 48 cores, 104 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 4090 24 GB. Secondary: macOS arm64 laptops. Users: Claude Code and Codex agent sessions on that host.
context: Two independent first-round reviewers read the same packet. Both kept ai-memory, agentmemory and deja-vu as finalists; one also kept Hindsight.
comparisons_on_record_where_every_named_: LongMemEval-S, session-level retrieval, 470 questions, recall_all@5, on a Mac (descriptive): agentmemory 0.9.29 with the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedder over its REST path 0.821; ai-memory (a 2.5 pre-release build) with Qwen3-Embedding-4B and its LLM reranker turned off 0.570; plain BM25 0.747. Not run: ai-memory with its LLM reranker, agentmemory through its Claude Code hooks, Hindsight 0.10.1 and MemPalace 3.10.0. The two systems captured different amounts of each session and used different embedders.

reviewer_notes.note: Provisional owner candidate: fullest documented fit to the requirement as written (typed Claude Code<->Codex handoffs, workspace/project scope, markdown-in-git capture, documented purge, backup and restore). A finalist for the deciding head-to-head, not a second memory owner to co-install.

cited_facts.shows: [documented] 'Why ai-memory' (lines 17-80): quit Claude Code and continue in Codex with a handoff that is 'typed, owned, claimed exactly once'; the source of truth is a git-backed wiki of plain .md files and the database is a rebuildable index; lifecycle hooks capture prompts and tool calls, sanitized at a typed privacy boundary; capture, search and handoffs need zero LLM calls. Support matrix (lines 100-140): Linux, macOS and Windows via WSL2 supported; Claude Code and Codex are first-party MCP and hook integrations 'kept honest by CI'.

[documented] Safety matrix and 'What deleted means' for purge-session, purge-project and delete-workspace: destructive cascades with a preview when --confirm is omitted. `backup --to` streams a tarball built from an online sqlite3 .backup plus the wiki. `restore --from` stages and verifies the archive and refuses while the server runs. `reindex` rebuilds the index from the markdown, and `restore-page` restores a page from its version chain.

[documented] wiki/ is a git repository checkpointed by every consolidation pass. Sessions, observations, handoffs, users and embeddings live only in the DB, so recovering them needs `ai-memory restore --from <tarball>`; restoring from a mirror repo means rsync plus reindex.

[documented, vendor's in-repo harness with commit, dataset sha256 and hardware per run] LongMemEval-S, 470 scored questions: hit@5 (any evidence session) 0.823 with the local all-MiniLM embedder (2026-09-01) and 0.815 (2026-09-21, 2.4 RC); zero-LLM FTS 0.666-0.668; recall@5 (fraction of evidence sessions) 0.680. Capture excerpts are bounded at a 2 KB privacy boundary.

[on record, descriptive, Mac] LongMemEval-S session-level recall_all@5 (470 questions): an ai-memory 2.5 pre-release with Qwen3-Embedding-4B and its LLM reranker off scored 0.570, below plain BM25 (0.747) and agentmemory (0.821). The reranker arm was not run, and the arms captured different amounts per session with different embedders. This is a measured retrieval deficit against this selection.

reviewer_notes.note: Challenger finalist with the strongest published memory-quality evidence and the richest learning layer (retain/recall/reflect, observations, knowledge pages). Its first-party Claude Code and Codex integration shares one bank per repo. Run it in the head-to-head as the sole owner; it needs an LLM for retain, local or hosted.

cited_facts.shows: [documented; paper submitted 2025-12-14 by the Hindsight authors (affiliations not checked), not an independent reproduction] With an open-source 20B backbone, Hindsight lifts overall accuracy on LongMemEval and LoCoMo from 39% (full-context baseline on the same backbone) to 83.6%. A larger backbone reaches 91.4% on LongMemEval and up to 89.61% on LoCoMo (vs 75.78% for the strongest prior open system). These measure conversational QA accuracy, not coding-session handoff.

[documented] Retain/recall/reflect; memory banks with strict isolation; a built-in per-bank MCP endpoint /mcp/{bank_id}/. The Coding Agents package wires Claude Code and Codex CLI. Over 25 LLM providers, including fully local ollama/lmstudio/llamacpp and the claude-code and openai-codex subscription providers. Supported Platforms: Linux x86_64/ARM64 and macOS Apple Silicon via Docker, pip and embedded pg0. The README claims independent reproduction by the VT Sanghani Center and The Washington Post; that claim was not verified here.

[documented] The default bankIdTemplate `coding-agent::{gitProject}` makes every agent share one bank per repo, scoped and shared across Claude Code and Codex. Curated knowledge pages cover architecture, conventions and in-flight work. Uninstall removes exactly what install added, and deleting the bank removes the only state the integration keeps (around line 1141).

[documented] Auto-recall on UserPromptSubmit and async auto-retain on Stop. MCP knowledge tools include agent_knowledge_delete_page. Dynamic bank IDs per agent, project or session. The local hindsight-embed daemon needs an LLM provider for fact extraction (openai, anthropic, gemini, groq, ollama, openai-codex, claude-code). The Codex README documents SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks.

[documented] `hindsight-admin backup` writes a consistent REPEATABLE READ snapshot covering banks, documents, memory units, mental models, webhooks and the audit log. `restore` deletes the target schema before import. `export-bank` writes a portable ZIP (embeddings are regenerated on import) and is read-only against a live instance. The 2026-09-22 blog adds bank clone, import and rename.

reviewer_notes.note: It has strong committed retrieval artifacts on LongMemEval-S (500 questions, with the dataset sha256): hit@5 97.2% and evidence-recall@5 91.0%. It also offers Claude Code and Codex handoff, resume and forget, and export/import sync, with no LLM. But its model is that 'the transcripts are the memory': there is no consolidation or curated write layer beyond `remember` and `promote`, so the deciding comparison's useful-write measure barely applies. It is the best extra arm for the recall head-to-head.

findings: Every observed-now fact holds, with expected drift: ai-memory went from 1851 to 1852 commits since 2026-07-03, its HEAD moved to ae1eabe7e0 (PENDING), and open issues are 12 rather than 13.

After review the selection lists four finalist arms for the deciding head-to-head, not a chosen owner: ai-memory, Hindsight and agentmemory as the judge picked, plus deja-vu promoted from the judge's recall-only arm to a full arm.

The evidence cannot separate the finalists, and the judge's own close_call says so. The only measured head-to-head on record ranks the provisional owner, ai-memory, last on recall_all@5: 0.570, against plain BM25 at 0.747 and agentmemory at 0.821. That run had ai-memory's reranker off and used different embedders. The self-published hit@5 and recall_any numbers come from separate harnesses and cannot be compared. Calling ai-memory the 'provisional owner' therefore rests on criterion 1 (capability fit) alone and should not be read as a measured lead.

The judge demoted deja-vu to a 'recall-only arm' partly by understating it. Its README documents a curated write layer. `deja promote <id>` distills a session into a curated note with provenance, tags and a lifecycle state, and these notes outrank raw transcripts (L198). `--state rejected` marks a reverted decision (L58), and `remember` stores a durable decision (L245). So the deciding comparison's useful-write measure does apply to it.

deja-vu also leads agentmemory on currency and maintenance: 2094 vs 51 default-branch commits since 2026-07-03, a latest release 2 days old vs 46 days, green CI, and 86 vs 314 open issues. It has first-party Claude Code and Codex handoff, resume and forget, plus export/import. It should run as a full finalist.

Not verified: whether deja-vu keeps its own copies of transcripts after Claude Code's cleanup deletes the originals. Its README raises this case (L526-528), but I did not resolve it. Its recovery path (sync export/import plus re-indexing transcripts) therefore depends on something unconfirmed, and the isolated-restore test in the head-to-head covers it.

Hindsight's README claim of independent reproduction (L50) is weaker than it sounds. The README itself calls the Virginia Tech Sanghani Center and Washington Post reproducers 'research collaborators'. The arXiv author list includes Naren Ramakrishnan and Xuan Wang; their Virginia Tech affiliation was not verified on the abs page. The paper's figures measure conversational QA accuracy, not coding-session handoff.

ai-memory churns heavily: 120 releases since 2026-05-21, 3 releases in the last 2 days, and two failing default-branch commits on 2026-10-01 (16:56Z and 17:03Z). That counts for currency, but it is a risk when choosing a version to pin.
The judgment does not use popularity or current use. The 'provisional owner' label is justified by documented fit.

critic.deciding_comparison: Run the judge's six-measure head-to-head on the new WSL2 host, with four arms. Install each one alone as the sole memory owner. (1) ai-memory, run with its LLM reranker on and off, using a matched embedder. (2) Hindsight, run once with a local model on the RTX 4090 and once with a hosted model. (3) agentmemory, through its Claude Code and Codex hooks path, not REST alone. (4) deja-vu as a full arm, including promote and remember notes. Measure: source-grounded recall and abstention over Claude Code -> Codex -> Claude Code chains in two projects; cross-project leakage; useful-write quality judged against the source transcripts; forget or purge, then confirm absence from both recall and indexes; backup -> fresh data dir -> restore, with recall compared for identity; and complete token, latency and cost usage, including LLM calls made during capture. As a secondary measure, report LongMemEval-S recall_all@5 with a matched embedder. The arm that leads on source-grounded recall while passing deletion and isolated restore becomes the single owner.
